version.changelog:
web-browser 0.2.3

- Updated documentation for credential issuance and browser backend environment detection.
- Clarified required environment variable checks for cmux detection, emphasizing multi-variable (OR) logic over single-variable detection.
- No functional or code changes; this version focuses on refining guides and changelogs for accuracy.

llm.summary: This browser automation skill also gives the agent broad authority to find, issue, extract, and store credentials, so users should review it carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: The UI testing and browser-routing purpose is coherent, and credential issuance is disclosed, but the credential workflow expands into local secret discovery, token extraction from authenticated pages, scope expansion, and downstream CLI handoff across cloud and developer accounts.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Several sensitive actions are mandatory or broadly framed, including checking .env files, project memory, Vault, and GitHub secrets, extracting token values, persisting credentials, and driving token-generation UI after user login without clear per-action consent gates.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No malicious install-time behavior was found: metadata lists markdown guidance plus one Playwright CDP helper script, static scan was clean, and VirusTotal telemetry was absent.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill may reuse a real logged-in browser session, inspect closed shadow DOM via CDP, run browser cleanup commands, and perform credential operations; those capabilities are high-trust and under-scoped for a general browser helper.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifacts make durable secret storage a required step, including Vault, GitHub secrets, keyrings, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.oci/config, .env files, and skill data, which creates lasting privileged access beyond the immediate browser task.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want a high-trust browser plus credential-management workflow. Before using it, require explicit approval for each secret source read, each token issuance or scope expansion, each token extraction, each storage destination, and any browser process/profile cleanup. Avoid using it on machines or projects with unrelated credentials unless the skill is revised to make secret access narrow, opt-in, and auditable.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] expected: CDP full-DOM and closed-shadow inspection is purpose-aligned for cascade debugging, but it should be limited on authenticated or sensitive pages because the artifact instructs broad DOM traversal.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The artifact-backed concern about checking skill data, project memory, .env, Vault, and GitHub secret stores before browser work is broader than a normal browser workflow and lacks clear user-controlled scoping.
[SDI-1] expected: Credential persistence is part of the stated credential-issuance purpose, but the mandatory multi-store matrix is too broad and durable without explicit opt-in per destination.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad trigger phrases such as browser test, open login screen, and issue token could route ordinary requests into a high-impact credential workflow.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The concerns about insufficient warnings are supported: the skill reuses logged-in sessions, reads secret sources, may collect tokens in chat-visible flows, accepts --login user:pass in the helper script, and includes destructive browser-profile recovery steps without prominent confirmation language.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The mandatory GitHub SSO preference for Microsoft-gated services removes user choice and could select the wrong identity in multi-account environments.
[SSD-3] expected: Handling issued tokens is inherent to the credential-issue topic, but the artifact directs raw token collection, snapshot extraction, mandatory persistence, and automation handoff in ways that raise long-term exposure risk.
[PE3] expected: References to keyrings, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.oci/config, .env, Vault, and GitHub secrets are related to credential persistence, but they materially broaden host and cloud privilege and should not be automatic.
